paragraphs.sourceText: Direction: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay commenting on the remark “A smile is the shortest distance between two people.” You can cite examples to illustrate your point. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
paragraphs.translationZh: 指导：这部分，你有30分钟的时间写一篇文章，评论“微笑是两个人之间最短的距离”这句话。你可以举一些例子来说明你的观点。你应该写至少150字但不超过200字。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you will hear 8 short conversations and 2 long conversations. At the end of each conversation, one or more questions will be asked about what was said. Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once. After each question there will be a pause. During the pause, you must read the four choices marked A)，B)，C) and D), and decide which is the best answer. Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 1 with a single line through the centre.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本部分中，您将听到 8 个短对话和 2 个长对话。每次对话结束时，都会针对谈话内容提出一个或多个问题。对话和问题都只会说一次。每个问题之后都会有一个暂停。在暂停期间，你必须阅读标有A)，B)，C)和D)的四个选项，并决定哪个是最佳答案。然后在答卷 1 上用一条穿过中心的线标记相应的字母。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 9 to 12 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the passage you have just heard.

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you will hear a passage three times. When the passage is read for the first time, you should listen carefully for its general idea. When the passage is read for the second time, you are required to fill in the blanks with the exact words you have just heard. Finally, when the passage is read for the third time, you should check what you have written.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将听到一段段落三遍。第一次读这篇文章时，你应该仔细听它的大意。当第二次阅读这篇文章时，你需要用你刚刚听到的单词填空。最后，当第三次阅读这篇文章时，你应该检查你所写的内容。

paragraphs.sourceText: The ideal companion machine would not only look, feel, and sound friendly but would also be programmed to behave in an agreeable manner. Those qualities that 26 other people enjoyable would be simulated as closely as possible, and the machine would appear to be 27 ,stimulating and easygoing. Its informal conversational style would make interaction comfortable, and yet the machine would remain slightly 28 and therefore interesting. In its first 29 , it might be somewhat hesitant and unassuming, but as it came to know the user it would progress to a more 30 and intimate style. The machine would not be a passive 31 but would add its own suggestions, information, and opinions; it would sometimes 32 in developing or changing the topic and would have a 33 of its own.

The machine would convey presence. We have all seen how a computer’s use of personal names often fascinates people and needs them to treat the machine as if it were almost human. Such features are easily written into the software. By introducing a degree of forcefulness and humour, the machine could 34 a vivid and unique character.

Friendships are not made in a day, and the computer would be more 35 as a friend if it simulated the gradual changes that occur when one person is getting to know another. At an appropriate time it might also express the kind of affection that stimulates attachment and intimacy.

Directions：In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word far each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：本节有一段有十个空格。您需要从文章后面的单词库中给出的选项列表中每个空白处选择一个单词。在做出选择之前仔细阅读该段落。银行中的每个选择都由一个字母标识。请在答题卡 2 上的每个项目上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。您不得多次使用银行中的任何单词。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 36 to 45 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 36 至 45 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Most experts in sleep behaviour agree that there is virtually an epidemic of sleepiness in the nation. “I can’t think of a 36 study that hasn’t found Americans getting less sleep than they ought to,” says Dr David.

The beginning of our sleep-deficit crisis can be 37 to the invention of the light bulb a century ago. From diary entries and other personal accounts from the 18th and 19th centuries, sleep scientists have reached the 38 that the average person used to sleep about 9.5 hours a night. By the 1950s and 1960s, that sleep schedule had been reduced 39 to between 7.5 and 8 hours, and most people had to wake to an alarm clock. “People cheat on their sleep, and they don’t realise they’re doing it,” says Dr David. “They think they’re okay because they can get by on 6.5 hours, when they really need 7.5, 8 or even more to feel 40 vigorous.”

Perhaps the most merciless robber of sleep, researchers say, is the 41 of the day. Whenever pressures from work, family, friends and community mount, many people consider sleep the least expensive item on the agenda. “In our society, you’re considered 42 if you say you only need 5.5 hours’ sleep. If you say you’ve got to get 8.5 hours, people think you lack drive and ambition.” To assess the 43 of sleep deficit, researchers have put subjects through a set of psychological and performance tests requiring them, for instance, to add columns of numbers or 44 a passage read to them only minutes earlier.
“We’ve found that if you’re sleep-deprived, performance suffers,” says Dr David. “Short-term memory is 45 , so are abilities to make decisions and to concentrate.”

Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2. Welcome, Freshmen. Have an iPod.
paragraphs.translationZh: 您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。欢迎，新生。有一个 iPod。

paragraphs.sourceText: A) Taking a step that many professors may view as a bit counterproductive, some colleges and universities are doling out Apple iPhones and Internet-capable iPods to their students. The always-on Internet devices raise some novel possibilities, like tracking where students gather together. With far less controversy, colleges could send messages about cancelled classes, delayed buses, campus crises or just the cafeteria menu.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 一些学院和大学采取了许多教授可能认为有点适得其反的措施，向学生分发苹果 iPhone 和具有互联网功能的 iPod。永远在线的互联网设备带来了一些新奇的可能性，比如跟踪学生聚集的地方。争议要少得多，大学可以发送有关取消课程、公交车延误、校园危机或只是自助餐厅菜单的信息。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) While schools emphasise its usefulness — online research in class and instant polling of students, for example 一a big part of the attraction is, undoubtedly, that the iPhone is cool and a hit with students. Being equipped with one of the most recent cutting-edge IT products could just help a college or university foster a cutting-edge reputation.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 虽然学校强调它的实用性——例如课堂上的在线研究和学生的即时投票——但毫无疑问，iPhone 的很大一部分吸引力在于它很酷并且很受学生欢迎。配备最新的尖端 IT 产品之一可以帮助学院或大学树立尖端声誉。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) Apple stands to win as well, hooking more young consumers with decades of technology purchases ahead of them. The lone losers, some fear, could be professors. Students already have laptops and cell phones, of course, but the newest devices can take class distractions to a new level. They practically beg a user to ignore the long-suffering professor struggling to pass on accumulated wisdom from the front of the room 一a prospect that teachers find most irritating and students view as, well, inevitable.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 苹果也将获胜，吸引更多年轻消费者购买数十年的技术产品。一些人担心，唯一的失败者可能是教授。当然，学生们已经拥有笔记本电脑和手机，但最新的设备可以将课堂干扰提升到一个新的水平。他们实际上恳求用户忽略长期受苦受难的教授，他在教室前面努力传递积累的智慧——教师们认为这种前景最令人恼火，而学生们则认为这是不可避免的。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) “When it gets a little boring, I might pull it out,” acknowledged Naomi Pugh, a first-year student at Freed-Hardeman University in Henderson, Tenn., referring to her new iPod Touch, which can connect to the Internet over a campus wireless network. She speculated that professors might try even harder to make classes interesting if they were to compete with the devices.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) “当它变得有点无聊时，我可能会把它拿出来，”田纳西州亨德森市弗里德哈德曼大学一年级学生 Naomi Pugh 承认，她指的是她的新 iPod Touch，它可以通过校园无线网络连接到互联网。她推测，如果教授们要与这些设备竞争，他们可能会更加努力地让课程变得有趣。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) Experts see a movement toward the use of mobile technology in education, though they say it is in its infancy as professors try to come up with useful applications. Providing powerful hand-held devices is sure to fuel debates over the role of technology in higher education. “We think this is the way the future is going to work” said Kyle Dickson, co-director of research and the mobile learning initiative at Abilene Christian University in Texas, which has bought more than 600 iPhones and 300 iPods for students entering this fall.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 专家们看到了在教育中使用移动技术的趋势，尽管他们表示，随着教授们试图提出有用的应用程序，这一趋势还处于起步阶段。提供强大的手持设备肯定会引发关于技术在高等教育中的作用的争论。德克萨斯州阿比林基督教大学研究和移动学习项目联合主任凯尔·迪克森 (Kyle Dickson) 表示：“我们认为这就是未来的发展方向。”该大学已为今年秋季入学的学生购买了 600 多部 iPhone 和 300 部 iPod。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) Although plenty of students take their laptops to class, they don’t take them everywhere and would prefer something lighter. Abilene Christian settled on the devices after surveying students and finding that they did not like hauling around their laptops, but that most of them always carried a cell phone, Dr Dickson said.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 虽然很多学生带着笔记本电脑去上课，但他们不会随身携带，并且更喜欢轻便的东西。迪克森博士说，阿比林·克里斯蒂安对学生进行了调查，发现他们不喜欢随身携带笔记本电脑，但他们中的大多数人总是随身携带手机，因此最终选择了这些设备。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) It is not clear how many colleges and universities plan to give out iPhones and iPods this fall; officials at Apple were
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 目前尚不清楚有多少所学院和大学计划在今年秋季发放 iPhone 和 iPod；苹果公司的官员是

paragraphs.sourceText: unwilling to talk about the subject and said that they would not leak any institution’s plans. “We can’t announce other people’s news,” said Greg Joswiak, vice president of iPod and iPhone marketing at Apple. He also said that he could not discuss discounts to universities for bulk purchases.
paragraphs.translationZh: 不愿意谈论这个话题，并表示不会泄露任何机构的计划。 “我们不能宣布其他人的消息，”苹果 iPod 和 iPhone 营销副总裁格雷格·乔斯维亚克 (Greg Joswiak) 说。他还表示，他无法讨论向大学批量购买的折扣。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) At least four institutions — the University of Maryland, Oklahoma Christian University, Abilene Christian and Freed-Hardeman 一have announced that they will give the devices to some or all of their students this fall. Other universities are exploring their options. Stanford University has hired a student-run company to design applications like a campus map and directory for the iPhone. It is considering whether to issue iPhones but not sure it’s necessary, noting that more than 700 iPhones were registered on the university’s network last year. At the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, iPhones might already have been everywhere, if AT&T, the wireless carrier offering the iPhone in the United States, had a more reliable network, said Andrew Yu, mobile devices platform project manager at MIT. “We would have probably gone ahead with this, maybe just getting a thousand iPhones and giving them out,” Mr. Yu said.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 至少有四家机构——马里兰大学、俄克拉荷马基督教大学、阿比林基督教大学和弗里德哈德曼大学——已经宣布，他们将在今年秋天向部分或全部学生提供这些设备。其他大学正在探索他们的选择。斯坦福大学聘请了一家学生经营的公司来设计 iPhone 校园地图和目录等应用程序。该校正在考虑是否发放 iPhone，但不确定是否有必要，并指出去年有 700 多部 iPhone 在该大学的网络上注册。麻省理工学院移动设备平台项目经理 Andrew Yu 表示，如果在美国提供 iPhone 的无线运营商 AT&T 拥有更可靠的网络，iPhone 可能已经无处不在。 “我们可能会继续这样做，也许只是购买 1000 部 iPhone 并分发出去，”于先生说。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) The University of Maryland at College Park is proceeding cautiously, giving the iPhone or iPod Touch to 150 students, said Jeffrey Huskamp, vice president and chief information officer at the university. “We don’t think that we have all the answers,” Mr. Huskamp said. By observing how students use the gadgets, he said, “We’re trying to get answers from the students.”
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 马里兰大学帕克分校副校长兼首席信息官 Jeffrey Huskamp 表示，该校正在谨慎行事，为 150 名学生提供了 iPhone 或 iPod Touch。 “我们认为我们并没有找到所有的答案，”赫斯坎普先生说。他说，通过观察学生如何使用这些设备，“我们试图从学生那里得到答案。”

paragraphs.sourceText: J) At each college, the students who choose to get an iPhone must pay for mobile phone service. Those service contracts include unlimited data use. Both the iPhones and the iPod Touch devices can connect to the Internet through campus wireless networks. With the iPhone, those networks may provide faster connections and longer battery life than AT&T’s data network. Many cell phones allow users, to surf the Web, but only some newer ones are capable of wireless connection to the local area computer network.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 在每所大学，选择购买 iPhone 的学生必须支付手机服务费。这些服务合同包括无限的数据使用。 iPhone和iPod Touch设备都可以通过校园无线网络连接到互联网。对于 iPhone，这些网络可能比 AT&T 的数据网络提供更快的连接和更长的电池寿命。许多手机允许用户上网冲浪，但只有一些较新的手机能够无线连接到局域网计算机网络。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) University officials say that they have no plans to track their students (and Apple said it would not be possible unless students give their permission). They say that they are drawn to the prospect of learning applications outside the classroom, though such lesson plans have yet to surface.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 大学官员表示，他们没有计划追踪学生（苹果公司表示，除非学生同意，否则不可能追踪）。他们表示，他们被课堂外学习应用的前景所吸引，尽管此类课程计划尚未浮出水面。

paragraphs.sourceText: L) “My colleagues and I are studying something called augmented reality (a field of computer research dealing with the combination of real-world and virtual reality)” said Christopher Dede, professor in learning technologies at Harvard University. “Alien Contact,” for example, is an exercise developed for middle-school students who use hand-held devices that can determine their location. As they walk around a playground or other area, text, video or audio pops up at various points to help them try to figure out why aliens were in the schoolyard.
paragraphs.translationZh: L）“我和我的同事正在研究一种叫做增强现实的东西（一个涉及现实世界和虚拟现实结合的计算机研究领域）”哈佛大学学习技术教授 Christopher Dede 说。例如，“外星人接触”是一项为中学生开发的练习，他们使用可以确定其位置的手持设备。当他们在操场或其他区域走动时，文字、视频或音频会在不同的地方弹出，以帮助他们试图弄清楚为什么外星人会出现在校园里。

paragraphs.sourceText: M) “You can imagine similar kinds of interactive activities along historical lines,” like following the Freedom Trail in Boston, Professor Dede said. “It’s important that we do research so that we know how well something like this works.”
paragraphs.translationZh: M）“你可以沿着历史路线想象类似的互动活动”，比如沿着波士顿的自由之路，德德教授说。 “重要的是我们要进行研究，这样我们才能知道这样的事情有多有效。”

paragraphs.sourceText: N) The rush to distribute the devices worries some professors, who say that students are less likely to participate in class if they are multi-tasking. “I’m not someone who’s anti-technology, but I’m always worried that technology becomes an end in and of itself, and it replaces teaching or it replaces analysis,” said Ellen Millender, associate professor of classics at Reed College in Portland, Ore. (She added that she hoped to buy an iPhone for herself once prices fall.) Robert Summers, who has taught at Cornell Law School for about 40 years, announced this week — in a detailed, footnoted memorandum 一that he would ban laptop computers from his class on contract law. “I would ban that too if I knew the students were using it in class,” Professor Summers said of the iPhone, after the device and its capabilities were explained to him. “What we want to encourage in these students is an active intellectual experience, in which they develop the wide range of complex reasoning abilities required of good lawyers.”
paragraphs.translationZh: N) 急于分发这些设备让一些教授感到担忧，他们说，如果学生同时处理多项任务，他们就不太可能参加课堂。俄勒冈州波特兰里德学院古典学副教授埃伦·米伦德 (Ellen Millender) 表示：“我不是反技术的人，但我总是担心技术本身会成为目的，它会取代教学或分析。”（她补充说，一旦价格下跌，她希望为自己购买一部 iPhone。）在康奈尔法学院任教约 40 年的罗伯特·萨默斯 (Robert Summers) 本周在一份详细的、带脚注的备忘录中宣布，他根据合同法，他的班级将禁止使用笔记本电脑。在向萨默斯教授解释了 iPhone 及其功能后，萨默斯教授谈到 iPhone 时表示：“如果我知道学生们在课堂上使用它，我也会禁止使用它。” “我们希望鼓励这些学生进行积极的智力体验，在其中培养优秀律师所需的广泛的复杂推理能力。”

paragraphs.sourceText: O) The experience at Duke University may ease some concerns. A few years ago, Duke began giving iPods to students with the idea that they might use them to record lectures (these older models could not access the Internet). “We had assumed that the biggest focus of these devices would be consuming the content,” said Tracy Futhey, vice president for
paragraphs.translationZh: O) 杜克大学的经历可能会缓解一些担忧。几年前，杜克大学开始向学生提供 iPod，希望他们可以用它们来录制讲座（这些旧型号无法访问互联网）。 “我们原以为这些设备的最大焦点是消费内容，”该公司副总裁 Tracy Futhey 说道。

paragraphs.sourceText: information technology and chief information officer at Duke. But that is not all that the students did. They began using the iPods to create their own “content”, making audio recordings of themselves and presenting them. The students turned what could have been a passive interaction into an active one, Ms Futhey said.
paragraphs.translationZh: 杜克大学信息技术和首席信息官。但这并不是学生们所做的全部。他们开始使用 iPod 创建自己的“内容”，录制自己的音频并进行展示。富西女士说，学生们将原本被动的互动变成了主动的互动。

paragraphs.sourceText: 46. University officials claim that they dole out iPhones and iPods so as to facilitate students’ learning outside of class.
paragraphs.translationZh: 46. 大学官员声称，他们发放 iPhone 和 iPod 是为了方便学生在课外学习。

paragraphs.sourceText: 47. In the author’s view, being equipped with IT products may help colleges and universities build an innovative image.
paragraphs.translationZh: 47. 在作者看来，配备信息技术产品可能有助于高校树立创新形象。

paragraphs.sourceText: 48. Professor Robert Summers at Cornell Law School banned laptop computers from his class because he thinks qualified lawyers need to possess a broad array of complex reasoning abilities.
paragraphs.translationZh: 48. 康奈尔大学法学院的罗伯特·萨默斯教授禁止在课堂上使用笔记本电脑，因为他认为合格的律师需要具备广泛的复杂推理能力。

paragraphs.sourceText: 49. Naomi Pugh at Freed-Hardeman University speculated that professors would have to work harder to enliven their classes.
paragraphs.translationZh: 49. 弗里德-哈德曼大学的内奥米·皮尤 (Naomi Pugh) 推测，教授们必须更加努力才能让课堂充满活力。

paragraphs.sourceText: 50. The University of Maryland at College Park is proceeding with caution concerning the use of iPhones and iPods.
paragraphs.translationZh: 50. 马里兰大学帕克分校对 iPhone 和 iPod 的使用持谨慎态度。

paragraphs.sourceText: 51. Many professors think that giving out Apple iPhones or Internet-capable iPods to students may not benefit education as intended.
paragraphs.translationZh: 51. 许多教授认为向学生赠送苹果 iPhone 或具有互联网功能的 iPod 可能不会像预期那样有利于教育。

paragraphs.sourceText: 52. The experience at Duke University may ease some concerns because the students have used iPods for active interaction.
paragraphs.translationZh: 52. 杜克大学的经历可能会缓解一些担忧，因为学生们已经使用 iPod 进行积极互动。

paragraphs.sourceText: 53. Ellen Millender at Reed College in Portland is concerned that technology will take the place of teaching or analysis.
paragraphs.translationZh: 53. 波特兰里德学院的 Ellen Millender 担心技术将取代教学或分析。

paragraphs.sourceText: 54. The distribution of iPhones among students has raised concerns that they will further distract students from class participation.

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 56 to 60 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 56 至 60 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: In 2011, many shoppers chose to avoid the frantic crowds and do their holiday shopping from the comfort of their computer. Sales at online retailers gained by more than 15%, making it the biggest season ever. But people are also returning those purchases at record rates, up 8% from last year.
paragraphs.translationZh: 2011 年，许多购物者选择避开疯狂的人群，在舒适的电脑上进行假日购物。在线零售商的销售额增长了 15% 以上，成为有史以来最大的销售季。但人们也以创纪录的速度退货，比去年增加了 8%。

paragraphs.sourceText: What went wrong? Is the lingering shadow of the global financial crisis making it harder to accept extravagant indulgences? Or that people shop more impulsively — and therefore make bad decisions — when online? Both arguments are plausible. However, there is a third factor: a question of touch. We can love the look but, in an online environment, we cannot feel the quality of a texture, the shape of the fit, the fall of a fold or, for that matter, the weight of an earring. And physically interacting with an object makes you more committed to your purchase.
paragraphs.translationZh: 出了什么问题？全球金融危机的阴影是否让人们更难以接受奢侈的放纵？或者人们在网上购物时更加冲动，从而做出错误的决定？这两种论点都是有道理的。然而，还有第三个因素：触摸问题。我们可以喜欢它的外观，但在网络环境中，我们无法感受到质地的质量、合身的形状、褶皱的脱落，或者就此而言，耳环的重量。与物体的身体互动会让你更加坚定地购买。

paragraphs.sourceText: When my most recent book Brandwashed was released, I teamed up with a local bookstore to conduct an experiment about the differences between the online and offline shopping experience. I carefully instructed a group of volunteers to promote my book in two different ways. The first was a fairly hands-off approach. Whenever a customer would inquire about my book, the volunteer would take him over to the shelf and point to it. Out of 20 such requests, six customers proceeded with the purchase.
paragraphs.translationZh: 当我的最新著作《Brandwashed》出版时，我与当地一家书店合作进行了一项有关线上和线下购物体验差异的实验。我小心翼翼地指导一群志愿者以两种不同的方式宣传我的书。第一种是相当不干涉的方法。每当顾客询问我的书时，志愿者就会把他带到书架上并指着它。在 20 个此类请求中，有 6 个客户继续购买。

paragraphs.sourceText: The second option also involved going over to the shelf but, this time, removing the book and then subtly holding onto it for just an extra moment before placing it in the customer’s hands. Of the 20 people who were handed the book, 13 ended up buying it. Just physically passing the book showed a big difference in sales. Why? We feel something similar to a sense of
paragraphs.translationZh: 第二种选择也涉及到书架，但这一次，将书取出，然后巧妙地握住它多一会儿，然后将其放在顾客手中。在收到这本书的 20 人中，有 13 人最终购买了它。仅仅通过实际传递这本书就可以看出销量的巨大差异。为什么？我们感受到了类似的感觉

paragraphs.sourceText: ownership when we hold things in our hand. That’s why we establish or reestablish connection by greeting strangers and friends with a handshake. In this case, having to then let go of the book after holding it might generate a subtle sense of loss, and motivate us to make the purchase even more.
paragraphs.translationZh: 当我们把东西握在手中时，所有权。这就是为什么我们通过握手来问候陌生人和朋友来建立或重新建立联系。在这种情况下，拿着书后必须放开可能会产生一种微妙的失落感，并激励我们更加购买。

paragraphs.sourceText: A recent study also revealed the power of touch, in this case when it came to conventional mail. A deeper and longer-lasting impression of a message was formed when delivered in a letter, as opposed to receiving the same message online. Brain imaging showed that, on touching the paper, the emotional centre of the brain was activated, thus forming a stronger bond. The study also indicated that once touch becomes part of the process, it could translate into a sense of possession. This sense of ownership is simply not part of the equation in the online shopping experience.
paragraphs.translationZh: 最近的一项研究还揭示了触摸的力量，在这种情况下，当涉及到传统邮件时。与在网上接收相同的信息相比，通过信件传递信息会形成更深刻、更持久的印象。脑成像显示，触摸纸张时，大脑的情感中心被激活，从而形成更牢固的联系。研究还表明，一旦触摸成为这个过程的一部分，它就可以转化为一种占有感。这种主人翁意识根本不属于在线购物体验的一部分。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 61 to 65 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 61 至 65 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Apparently everyone knows that global warming only makes climate more extreme. A hot, dry summer has triggered another flood of such claims. And, while many interests are at work, one of the players that benefits the most from this story are the media: the notion of “extreme” climate simply makes for more compelling news.
paragraphs.translationZh: 显然每个人都知道全球变暖只会使气候变得更加极端。炎热干燥的夏季再次引发了此类说法的泛滥。而且，虽然许多利益都在发挥作用，但从这个故事中受益最大的参与者之一是媒体：“极端”气候的概念只会带来更引人注目的新闻。

paragraphs.sourceText: Consider Paul Krugman, writing breathlessly in The New York Times about the “rising incidence of extreme events”. He claims that global warming caused the current drought in America’s Midwest, and that supposedly record-high corn prices could cause a global food crisis.
paragraphs.translationZh: 想想保罗·克鲁格曼（Paul Krugman），他在《纽约时报》上气喘吁吁地写道“极端事件发生率不断上升”。他声称，全球变暖导致了美国中西部目前的干旱，而据称创纪录的玉米价格可能会引发全球粮食危机。

paragraphs.sourceText: But the United Nations climate panel’s latest assessment tells us precisely the opposite: For “North America, there is medium confidence that there has been an overall slight tendency towards less dryness”. Moreover, there is no way that Krugman could have identified this drought as being caused by global warming without a time machine: Climate models
paragraphs.translationZh: 但联合国气候小组的最新评估告诉我们恰恰相反：对于“北美来说，有中等信心认为总体上有轻微的干旱趋势”。此外，如果没有时间机器，克鲁格曼不可能确定这次干旱是由全球变暖引起的：气候模型

paragraphs.sourceText: estimate that such detection will be possible by 2048, at the earliest.
paragraphs.translationZh: 估计这种检测最早将在 2048 年实现。

paragraphs.sourceText: And, fortunately, this year’s drought appears unlikely to cause a food crisis, as global rice and wheat supplies remain plentiful. Moreover, Krugman overlooks inflation: Prices have increased, six-fold since 1969, so, while corn futures（期货） did set a record of about $8 per bushel（蒲式耳）in late July, the inflation-adjusted price of corn was higher throughout most of the 1970s, reaching $16 in 1974.
paragraphs.translationZh: 幸运的是，今年的干旱似乎不太可能引发粮食危机，因为全球大米和小麦供应仍然充足。此外，克鲁格曼忽视了通货膨胀：价格自 1969 年以来已经上涨了六倍，因此，虽然玉米期货确实在 7 月底创下了每蒲式耳 8 美元左右的纪录，但在 1970 年代的大部分时间里，经过通货膨胀调整的玉米价格都较高，在 1974 年达到了 16 美元。

paragraphs.sourceText: Finally, Krugman conveniently forgets that concerns about global warming are the main reason that com prices have skyrocketed since 2005. Nowadays 40 percent of com grown in the United States is used to produce ethanol (乙醇), which does absolutely nothing for the climate, but certainly distorts the price of com — at the expense of many of the worlds poorest people.
paragraphs.translationZh: 最后，克鲁格曼很容易忘记，对全球变暖的担忧是自 2005 年以来玉米价格飙升的主要原因。如今，美国种植的 40% 玉米用于生产乙醇 (乙醇)，这对气候绝对没有任何帮助，但肯定扭曲了玉米的价格，而牺牲了世界上许多最贫困人口的利益。

paragraphs.sourceText: Bill McKibben similarly worries in The Guardian about the Midwest drought and com prices. He confidently tells us that raging wildfires from New Mexico and Colorado to Siberia are “exactly” what the early stages of global warming look like.
paragraphs.translationZh: 比尔·麦基本 (Bill McKibben) 在《卫报》上也对中西部干旱和玉米价格表示担忧。他自信地告诉我们，从新墨西哥州、科罗拉多州到西伯利亚肆虐的野火“正是”全球变暖的早期阶段。

paragraphs.sourceText: In fact, the latest overview of global wildfire incidence suggests that fire intensity has declined over the past 70 years and is now close to its preindustrial level.
paragraphs.translationZh: 事实上，对全球野火发生率的最新概述表明，过去 70 年来火灾强度有所下降，目前已接近工业化前的水平。

paragraphs.sourceText: When well-meaning campaigners want us to pay attention to global warming, they often end up pitching beyond the facts. And, while this may seem justified by a noble goal, such “policy by panic” tactics rarely work, and often backfire.
paragraphs.translationZh: 当善意的活动家希望我们关注全球变暖时，他们往往会提出超出事实的说法。而且，虽然这似乎有一个崇高的目标，但这种“恐慌政策”策略很少奏效，而且常常适得其反。

paragraphs.sourceText: Remember how, in the wake of Hurricane Katrina in 2005, A1 Gore claimed that we were in store for ever more destructive hurricanes? Since then, hurricane incidence has dropped off the charts. Exaggerated claims merely fuel public distrust and disengagement.
paragraphs.translationZh: 还记得 2005 年卡特里娜飓风过后，A1 Gore 声称我们即将面临更具破坏性的飓风吗？从那时起，飓风发生率急剧下降。夸大的说法只会加剧公众的不信任和脱离接触。

paragraphs.sourceText: That is unfortunate, because global warming is a real problem, and we do need to address it.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这是不幸的，因为全球变暖是一个真正的问题，我们确实需要解决它。
